P1-01.title: _calib.py does not compute the max-over-families radius that graphlets.py says ORBIT5_RADIUS is; six hop-1 5-node orbit columns are tagged one rung too shallow
P1-01.concrete_trigger: _calib.calibrate records `radius[k] = r` only `if agree[k] and radius[k] == 0`, and then, INSIDE the per-graph loop, pins every still-unresolved seen orbit to max_r+1. Together these make the first graph that observes an orbit fix its radius permanently; later graphs cannot raise it. influence/graphlets.py (comment above ORBIT5_RADIUS) states the opposite: 'The value per orbit is the MAXIMUM over several graph families, since a dense graph whose 2-ball already covers everything will understate the radius.' _calib_edge.calibrate_edge has the identical structure.
P1-01.evidence: audit_p1_calib_probe.py 5 (scratchpad, 2026-09-11): (1) calibrate() over [ER,BA,HK] vs [HK,BA,ER] differs on orbits [56,57,65,66,68,70] -- a maximum is order-invariant, this is not. (2) Per-family radii: ER gives 1 for all six; BA and HK both give 2. Explicit max = 2. (3) The shipped ORBIT5_RADIUS gives 1 for exactly those six and agrees with the true max on every other seen orbit; orbit 72 (K5 centre) is never observed on the fixtures and is correctly 1 by hand. (4) cache_registry_ca-GrQc.csv registers orbit_56_g5, orbit_57_g5, orbit_65_g5, orbit_66_g5, orbit_68_g5, orbit_70_g5 at hop 1. Those six are 6 of the 17 five-node orbit columns admitted at r=1. The 4-node table is unaffected: all three families agree on all 15 orbits (audit_p1_calib_probe.py 4), which is why the documented validation against the hand table passed without exposing the aggregation.
P1-01.consequence: At r=1 the subgraph-inclusive tiers include six columns that the project's own operational definition, measured on two of the three calibration families, says a radius-1 observer cannot compute. This is the failure class recorded in the vault (brain/Gotchas.md, 'Tier tags are inputs, not labels', Finding 10). It bears directly on the Lane 4 r=1 ablation written up on 2026-09-10 (study_doc_v2 s26k.3), whose headline is that the 5-node orbit rung carries the entire r=1 effect (17/20 contrasts flagged): six of that rung's seventeen columns are the mis-tagged ones. It also touches the r=1 cells of every subgraph-inclusive tier in all five sweeps and in the structural and buffered lanes. Direction of bias: including a column the observer could not have computed can only inflate the r=1 rung; magnitude is UNMEASURED.
P1-01.what_is_not_established: That these six orbits are non-computable at radius 1 on the five real networks; the calibration fixtures are n=50-60 synthetic graphs. The project's stated discipline is the conservative tag regardless ('never shallower'), so the tag is wrong under the project's own rule even before that measurement. Whether correcting the tag changes the 17/20 flag count or any headline is unmeasured and requires refitting the affected r=1 cells (see repair_column_order.py for why a registry retag is a refit, not a relabel).
P1-01.proposed_fix: (a) In _calib.calibrate and _calib_edge.calibrate_edge, aggregate with an explicit per-graph radius and take the maximum across graphs, moving the max_r+1 pin outside the graph loop. (b) Re-measure both 5-node tables with the corrected aggregation, over at least the existing three families, and diff against the shipped tables. (c) Retag 56,57,65,66,68,70 to hop 2 in graphlets.py and every cache_registry_*.csv, with a dated comment. (d) Evict and refit the r=1 cells of every tier that includes subgraph features, all targets, all seeds, all five networks; the r=1 ablation's top two rungs; and the r=1 cells of the structural and buffered lanes. (e) Re-score s26k.3 and reconcile the prose by graph. verify_pipeline.py's sweep_*.columns.json fingerprint will fail on the retag until (d) is done, which is the intended guard. Item (d) is a training run and needs Rachit's authorisation under the 2026-08-27 no-CPU-training decision as amended 2026-09-08.

P1-02.title: No content hash binds cached stage-1/2 results to the edge list they were computed from
P1-02.concrete_trigger: stage1_prepare.py writes cache_meta_<tag>.json with provenance counts, beta_c, p, versions and seed, but no SHA-256 of the input file; tag is `path.stem`, so any file with the same stem addresses the same cache namespace. Neither stage nor run_experiment.py imports hashlib (grep, 2026-09-11). data/manifest.json does carry a per-network sha256, but its only readers use it for paths, and fetch_data.fetch() on an already-present file simply re-hashes whatever is on disk and records that -- there is no expected-hash table, so a modified or corrupted local file is re-manifested rather than detected.
P1-02.evidence: Protocol review question 1 ('Can input identities change without invalidating cached or resumed results?') answers YES for stage 0/1/2. Mitigation that DOES exist: the five manifest hashes match the five data files on disk today (probe, 2026-09-11), and the Phase 6 lanes bind their own inputs (results/phase6_precision_input_preflight.json, provenance_*.json). The gap is upstream of those.
P1-02.consequence: A swapped or edited data/<tag>.txt sharing the stem would be silently paired with an existing cache on resume. No evidence any such swap occurred; the five registered networks reproduce their cached beta_c to 1e-7 (verify_criticality.check_registered_cache_thresholds), which is an indirect identity check on the graph.
P1-02.proposed_fix: Record input sha256, byte count and parsed row count in cache_meta_<tag>.json at stage 1; have stage 2 and run_experiment refuse to resume when the recorded hash differs from the file on disk; give fetch_data a pinned expected-hash table so a re-run verifies rather than re-records. None of this changes any number.

P1-03.title: multi_edges_collapsed counts reciprocated arcs from bidirectional source files as multi-edges
P1-03.concrete_trigger: build_network computes n_multi = len(edges) - len(edges_unique) AFTER np.sort(edges, axis=1) has folded (u,v) and (v,u) together, so every reciprocated arc pair is counted as a collapsed multi-edge.
P1-03.evidence: cache_meta_ca-GrQc.json: raw_edge_rows 28,980, self_loops_removed 12, multi_edges_collapsed 14,484 = (28,980-12)/2 exactly -- the SNAP file lists every edge in both directions and contains no genuine multi-edges. Same pattern on ca-HepTh (25,973 = (51,971-25)/2) and email-Eu-core (8,865). facebook_combined and p2p-Gnutella08 report 0. Note the manifest's directed_in_source flag does NOT predict this: ca-GrQc is flagged undirected yet ships both arcs.
P1-03.consequence: The graph is correct; only the audit-trail label is wrong. Any methods-section sentence that quotes 'multi-edges collapsed' for these three networks overstates the input's messiness. No numerical result depends on n_multi.
P1-03.proposed_fix: Count duplicates before the orientation sort (true multi-edges), and separately count reciprocated pairs; record both. Documentation-only impact.

P1-05.title: leading_eigenvalue raises an uncaught ArpackNoConvergence on small near-critical multicyclic graphs
P1-05.concrete_trigger: spla.eigs(M, k=1, which='LM', tol=1e-8) with no maxiter, ncv or dense fallback. On a theta graph (two hubs joined by three paths of L internal nodes) with L >= 10, n = 32, ARPACK fails to converge (3,281 iterations, 0/1 converged) and the exception propagates out of epidemic_threshold.
P1-05.evidence: audit_p1_criticality_probe2.py: theta10..theta24, with and without 40 disjoint tree components, all raise ArpackNoConvergence; the exact rho(B) from the dense 2m x 2m operator is 1.06-1.26 in every case. It NEVER returns a wrong value -- the failure is loud. The forest is irrelevant to the failure (the magnitude-1 tree roots are not what breaks it).
P1-05.consequence: A legitimate small sparse input crashes stage 1 with a third-party traceback instead of the module's designed ValueError. Not reachable from the registered corpus (all five networks and every stage-0 family are well above criticality at mean degree ~6) and not a correctness defect: no threshold is mis-reported.
P1-05.proposed_fix: For 2n below a few thousand, fall back to dense np.linalg.eigvals on ArpackNoConvergence (or use it outright); otherwise catch and re-raise as a ValueError naming the graph. Add a theta-graph fixture to verify_criticality.py.

P1-07.title: ORCA reports init failures with exit code 0 and an already-created empty output file, so the Python boundary's primary check cannot see them
P1-07.concrete_trigger: orca.cpp main() returns 0 after 'Stopping!' when init() fails, and init() opens the output file BEFORE validating the graph. graphlets.count_node_orbits / count_edge_orbits test `returncode != 0 or not exists(fout)`, which is False on every init failure.

P1-07.proposed_fix: Treat a zero-byte output file, or a non-empty stderr, as failure in graphlets.py; optionally patch orca.cpp's main to return 1 on init failure (a vendored change, to be recorded).

P1-10.concrete_trigger: The brief asked whether the bipartite-sign / tree-unit-root / unicyclic repair is correct AND complete, and whether leaving caches un-regenerated is safe.

P3-01.title: 2-sd star rule mis-stated as 'roughly alpha = 0.046'; it is |t| > 6.32, alpha ~ 1.4e-4, and 'zero stars withdrawn by BH' is forced by arithmetic
P3-01.concrete_trigger: analyse_multiplicity.py docstring lines 7-14 and line 202 (expected_null = 0.046 * n); RESULTS_multiplicity.txt 'expected under a global null : 2.8' printed four times; study section 19b lines 1139-1142; make_fig6.py docstring line 6.
P3-01.evidence: On n=10 paired seeds |mean| > 2*sd(ddof=1) is |t_9| > 2*sqrt(10) = 6.325. scipy: two-sided P(|t_9| > 2) = 0.0766 (so even the '2 sd = alpha 0.046' reading is wrong; 0.046 is P(|z|>2)); P(|t_9| > 6.325) = 1.369e-4. Expected false stars under a global null: 3204*1.37e-4 = 0.44 over the corpus, 0.008 per 60-comparison family - not 147 and not 'about three'. Every starred row has p_t <= 1.37e-4 (max observed 1.08e-4), and the smallest BH threshold in a family of 60 at q=0.05 is 0.05/60 = 8.3e-4, so a starred row can never fail BH: 'starred, NOT BH-significant = 0' is a theorem about the rule, not a result about the data. Section 19b itself states '|t| > 6.3, three times stricter' three paragraphs after asserting alpha = 0.046, so the section contradicts itself.
P3-01.consequence: The objection paragraph of section 19b overstates the null expectation by ~300x and the 'nothing is withdrawn' headline is presented as an empirical outcome of BH when it is guaranteed. The substantive conclusions are unaffected: no star is withdrawn (true, and now known to be necessarily true), 31 BH-significant comparisons are unstarred (true - the under-claiming direction is the real finding), and 'a claim needs both a q-value and an effect size' stands.
P3-01.what_is_not_established: Whether the paired t-test p-values are themselves well calibrated at n=10 (normality unverifiable; the sign test floor is reported alongside) - unchanged from the existing flagged assumption.
P3-01.proposed_fix: Reword the docstring, the printed expected_null (use n * 2*sf(2*sqrt(n)) from the t distribution, or state the star rule's implied alpha explicitly), section 19b's objection paragraph, and make_fig6's docstring; state plainly that stars are a subset of BH by construction and that the finding is the 31 unstarred effects. Regenerate RESULTS_multiplicity.txt from the script (no fits) at the same time as P3-07.

P3-02.title: analyse_c3_benchmarks.shares() uses the asymptotic tau-b floor while analyse_betweenness and c4_two_numbers use the exact form; docstring claims an identity assertion that is not made

P3-02.evidence: Recomputed both forms for the five project graphs: ca-GrQc 0.592875 (exact) vs 0.592850 (shares); ca-HepTh 0.571415/0.571404; p2p 0.418111/0.418104; email 0.259786/0.259769; facebook 0.155605/0.155604 - w identical. For the 14 C3 graphs from results_c3_structure.csv the exact-minus-shares difference is at most 1.54e-6 (soc-Epinions1), minimum 8.3e-10. Minimum |tau_all - (tau_floor + 0.05)| over all 5608 cells is 1.676e-4, so no P3 verdict is within reach of the O(1/n) discrepancy. The N10 pins in verify_pipeline.py are at 3 decimals (e.g. ca-GrQc 0.593) and pass under either form.

P3-02.proposed_fix: Use the exact form in shares() (one-line change, then re-review at the new hash) and correct the docstring; re-running the C3 traversal is NOT required to justify this because the floor is recomputable from results_c3_structure.csv, but the cells CSV tau_floor column would need regenerating to match - decision for Rachit.
